blocks.content: Course: Rapid Build With Claude Code
CI/CD stands for Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment. In SpeedBlip's setup, it means:

items: Continuous Integration: Every push to GitHub runs the build process (yarn build) automatically. If TypeScript finds a type error or the build fails, Netlify reports the failure and the previous working deploy stays live.
Continuous Deployment: If the build passes, Netlify automatically deploys the new version to the live URL.

blocks.content: This pipeline is why every SpeedBlip chunk ends with a git commit and push. The commit is not just a save point - it is a deployment. After pushing, I could open the live Netlify URL and verify the chunk's work on a real production build, not just a local dev server.

The difference matters. Vite's local dev server sometimes behaves differently from the production build (especially for environment variables, asset paths, and service worker registration). Testing on the live Netlify deploy after each chunk caught two issues during the SpeedBlip build that local testing missed entirely.

blocks.alt: Loop diagram showing: Commit and Push - Netlify Build Runs - Build Passes or Fails - If passes: Deploy to Live URL - If fails: Previous deploy stays live - Developer fixes and pushes again
